title: Local dimension-corrected resolution invariant: maximum-stratum calculus and termination
statement:
Over $\mathbf Q$, let $X\hookrightarrow P$ be a closed immersion with $X$ reduced and $P$ smooth, separated and of finite type [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. An admissible history is a finite initial segment of the maximum-stratum construction in (4), or a restriction or smooth ambient pullback of such a segment, deleting empty-center stages. It retains the ordinary ambient blowups, their centers, the successive scheme-theoretic strict transforms of $X$, and the order of the exceptional hypersurfaces created by those blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-nagata-strict-transform]. Initially the history is empty. There exist one totally ordered set $V\cup\{\bot\}$ with least element $\bot$ and, simultaneously for all such pairs $X\hookrightarrow P$ (including their finite disjoint unions) and all their admissible histories $H$, local invariant functions $\nu_H:|X_H|\to V\cup\{\bot\}$ with properties (1)--(4) below; the dimension-corrected Bierstone--Milman Hilbert--Samuel construction provides such functions. The values are normalized for smooth factors: they are synchronization values, rather than the raw Hilbert--Samuel functions or the unnormalized global-dimension-dependent first entries of $\operatorname{inv}^{\#}$. In particular, adding a smooth affine-space factor does not change the synchronization value. The properties are the following.

(1) Their image on each finite-type $X_H$ is finite. A point has value $\bot$ exactly when its local ring is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. If $X_H$ is not regular, its maximum value $m$ is greater than $\bot$; the locus $\{\nu_H=m\}$, with its reduced closed subscheme structure, is a nonempty regular closed subscheme $M_H\subset X_H$, nowhere dense in $X_H$. Here nowhere dense means that the underlying closed set contains no nonempty open subset. The ideals of $M_H$ on $X_H$ and on $P_H$ are coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Blowing up this center in $P_H$ gives an allowed next history; the new ambient scheme is again smooth, separated and finite type, the new strict transform is reduced, and its maximum invariant value, if greater than $\bot$, is strictly less than $m$.

(2) The same local construction is defined after restricting such a history to an open, and after smooth ambient pullback, including the deletion of empty-center stages. At corresponding points its values agree, without a constant-relative-dimension assumption. The reduced ideal of a maximum stratum pulls back to the reduced ideal of the inverse-image stratum (or the unit ideal for an empty stratum). These assertions concern each finite history and each individual stratum; termination is the separate clause (4).

(3) Suppose two such histories have isomorphic strict-transform schemes over their initial schemes, identifying at every earlier stage the center ideals on those strict transforms and their order. Then the two functions $\nu_H$ on the identified strict transforms agree, including their value set and the reduced ideals of all maximum strata. This includes histories in different smooth ambient embeddings and histories transported by an isomorphism of the initial reduced scheme. The comparisons commute with restriction and with pullback of the histories. The exceptional data on $X_H$ retain the inverse images of the earlier center ideals, even when an intrinsic blowup is an identity morphism.

(4) Termination. Starting with the empty history of any such pair, extend the history, as long as the current strict transform $X_H$ is not regular, by the ordinary blowup in the current ambient scheme of the reduced full maximum stratum $M_H$ of (1), and take the scheme-theoretic strict transform. There is no infinite sequence of such extensions. This includes finite disjoint unions and the empty initial scheme. It is a termination assertion for these particular functions $\nu_H$, not a claim that an arbitrary totally ordered set with strictly decreasing maxima is well founded.

proof.text: Choose a numerical engine using [lem-trf-marked-ideal-numerical-resolution-engine], and then choose its simultaneous normalized assignment using [lem-trf-normalized-resolution-word-gluing]. The latter provides finite image and regularity detection on every admissible history, for the same fixed word space and the same engine. Construct the calculus first on this small word type. At the end use the order-preserving injection into its universe lift: a range has the same greatest values after lifting, maximum steps are equivalent, and induction on the three admissibility constructors identifies admissible histories. Transport all fields along this injection to place the value type in Type (u+1), without changing any center or history.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13; re-split assembly step 1 of the normalized word construction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-resolution-word-finite-history-comparison] at the last stage to obtain smooth, separated, finite-type ambient geometry and a reduced intrinsic scheme for every admissible history, including histories obtained by smooth pullback with deletion. The progress theorem [lem-trf-resolution-word-progress-termination] now supplies maximum extensions and preservation of geometry. A positive next maximum implies nonregularity by bottom detection, so its strict inequality is the progress theorem. For an arbitrary maximum extension, uniqueness of the greatest value identifies its center support with the closed maximum supplied by [lem-trf-resolution-word-maximum-center-descent]. The actual center is reduced by the definition of maximum step. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] therefore gives an isomorphism with the regular nonempty reduced maximum center, and the support equality gives nowhere density. The ambient is locally Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; the preceding ambient of the extension is isomorphic to it, and the intrinsic scheme is a closed subscheme. On these locally Noetherian schemes ideal sheaves are quasi-coherent and finite type, hence have finite-type kernels of finite-free maps by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. This gives both required coherence fields in their existing encoding.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13; re-split assembly step 2 of the normalized word construction.

proof.text: Use the pullback existence clause of [lem-trf-resolution-word-finite-history-comparison]. Specialize its word and ideal comparisons to the final stage. The final prefix is definitionally the original history; the final-index equality transports the given stage map to SmoothPullback.finalMap. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], any reduced stratum ideal is the vanishing ideal of its closed support. The stagewise smooth ideal equality thus gives reducedness of its comap; the support-comap identity and value equality give its stratum condition. If the inverse-image equality locus is empty, the support is empty and the comapped ideal is the unit ideal. Intrinsic comparison gives final value equality. The final intrinsic isomorphism is surjective, so a greatest value on the second history is greatest on the first as well. The intrinsic vanishing-ideal equality then identifies any two reduced maximum-stratum ideals. These pointwise equalities are compatible with restriction and further pullback as in the comparison theorem.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13; re-split assembly step 3 of the normalized word construction.

proof.text: For (4), use [lem-trf-resolution-word-progress-termination] for this same assignment and the full maximum centers just identified. It rules out infinitely many head drops and an infinite constant-head tail, hence an infinite sequence from the empty history. The assertion includes finite disjoint unions, and the empty or regular input has zero steps. This is termination of the chosen construction; no additional well-foundedness assumption on its value space is needed.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13; re-split assembly step 4 of the normalized word construction.
